Furiae Sentinel, Vol. 32, Issue 129 - News in the Gauntleted City

Yesterday, Furiae naval forces soundly defeated a group of tanar'ri pirates that had been plaguing trade in and out of our ports. With assistance from our baatezu forces, Captain Yenn Corano soundly routed the demons, sinking their ships and picking deserters out of the sky.
An official Proclamation was made in the courts of Hellroost yesterday, as House Cascare condemned the illegal sale and use of the dangerous substance known on the streets as "worldwine."

Lady Ovida Cascare herself read the proclamation to the court, which called for increased vigilance and harsher penalties for anyone found using, possessing, or selling the arcane concoction. Guard patrols and random searches will increase throughout the city until this plague can be ended.
Worldwine is known to be very dangerous to those who imbibe it, causing paralyzation, hallucinations, and death. All citizens of the city are cautioned against its use.
Nonetheless, since the substance appeared on Furiae streets a few months ago, its use has reportedly grown greatly, especially in areas such as Rathole, where other illegal activity often flourishes.

Upstanding citizens of our city are cautioned against travelling to these districts or speaking to anyone who seems suspicious or unfamiliar. The Furiae City Guard is in the midst of investigating its origins and distribution. Any tips or information brought to them will be rewarded.

This victory is not only a victory against the forces of chaos that surround us. It is an assertion of dominance over Furiae's corner of the Outer Sea, our new home since the Arrival. It is an assertion that despite our "prime" origins, we will not be walked over by the planars that now surround us. We will hold to our way of life.

"There are those who think that because we are new to these parts, that we will submit to the unknown," Vice Admiral Yenn Corano stated. "Today, we have proven that we are as strong here as we were before the Arrival. We have proven that Furiae deserves its place here, and we will continue to thrive." The Corano noble family has long had a proud military tradition in Furiae, and Captain Yenn is a shining example of service to the city.

The defeat of the tanar'ri also represents a victory for our baatezu allies in nearby Avernus, in their long-running Blood War against the forces of chaos. We rejoice and give thanks to Zariel to whom Furiae owes so much, for such stout and powerful allies!

The city of Furiae has come through tense times since the Arrival, as terrorists continued to fight against our lawful rulers and, as we all know, this necessitated stricter laws and constant vigilance to keep order. That of course changed four years ago when the gates -- and doors -- of our glorious City were once again opened, allowing travel and trade across our new home in the Outlands and the planes beyond.

When the gates opened, travellers from across the planes came to our city for the scent of opportunity and the comfort of order. Among these, the Harmonium, a planar faction dedicated to order and law.

At first their relationship with the City Guard was a matter of contention, as both appeared to be acting separately towards the same goals. Over time, however, it became clear that there was more that united us than divided us.

Over the past few weeks, Sentinel reporters have spoken to members of both organizations and learned that high-ranking City Guards have been meeting with the Harmonium brass in an attempt to delineate roles and responsibilities, as any ordered society should have. These meetings have reportedly gone well, though are ongoing.

In the meantime, citizens are encouraged to treat the Harmonium with the same respect for authority as they afford our own guard, and to thank these hard-working men and women for helping to keep our city safe and law-abiding.
Naval Victory Secures Safety -- and Dominance
Proclamation Made Against Dangerous Substance on the Streets
Furiae Sentinel, Vol. 32, Issue 130 - News in the Gauntleted City

Reports from Court suggest that our illustrious rulers are considering allowing the opening of an official embassy to Sigil in Furiae. The office would take over the now-defunct Great Kingdom Embassy buildings in Midtown.

Since the Arrival, Furiae's citizens have been faced with a new reality in the Outer Planes. For several years, our gates were closed to the outside for safety as the city adjusted to its new place and the alliance between House Cascare and our Baatezu allies was secured. Four years ago, the wise decision was made to open the gates to the wider multiverse.

Since that event, planar travellers have come to our city bringing trade and prosperity -- as long as they have abided by our ways. These have included the Harmonium and Fraternity of Order, who have been welcomed into our fair City in exchange for their assistance maintaining the law, our law.
Citizens are cautioned that travel to Sigil and beyond is still a regulated activity. Proper requests must be filed before travel, and any new doors must be reported to authorities immediately.

But given the wide variety of planars who have expressed interest in visiting, trading with, or moving to Furiae, House Cascare has considered the need for some type of Planar Embassy, to help adjust those visitors to our ways, and inform our people of the realities of our new home. Those plans have begun to move bravely forward.
Early yesterday, a dangerous act of terrorism was perpetrated in the Sea Market. A warehouse near the docks of the district suddenly exploded, raining debris and fire on the surrounding area.

This act was no doubt enacted by the dangerous revolutionary elements that still exist in our city, anarchists with ties to the rebellion from before the Arrival. Such acts target the safety and security that make our city function, sowing chaos and fear. These revolutionaries must be brought to justice, security in the area will be increased.

Some witnesses report a gnome and other suspects fleeing the scene. Others suggest a fire elemental may have been released in the area. Until the truth can be determined and the perpetrators brought to justice, security in the area will be increased.
Anyone with information is encouraged to bring it to Officer Lucenna of the City Guard, who is spearheading the investigation from the Sea Market guard post. Any viable information will be rewarded.
Talks of Sigilian Embassy to Open in Midtown
Furiae Sentinel, Vol. 32, Issue 131 - News in the Gauntleted City
The Griffin Bank has announced plans to fund an expedition into the Outlands in the coming days.
Today, Furiae wakes to horror. Several members of House Corano, including its matriarch Cassandra Corano, and two children, were murdered in their own home during the night.

The Sentinel received an anonymous note of this horrendous event early in the morning as City Guards rushed to the scene to investigate. Early indications suggest a professional assassin, and Furiae Navy Vice Admiral Yenn Corano believes it may have been the act of revolutionaries in the city -- or perhaps even foreign planar interests.

"We know there are rebel elements who haven't given up despite the obvious need for order in our new reality, and otherworldly forces of chaos probe at our borders," the Vice Admiral said. "These elements wish to sow chaos in our city. I will not stand by and let them."

House Corano has been an institution of Furiae for over a century. Much of the modern development of the city has been through Corano investment. The Sea Market was originally a Corano development before it was generously sold to the city for redistribution. House Corano still owns and operates many of the piers and warehouses, patriotically supporting the business and economy there. They have also proven themselves great patrons of the arts, bringing more culture to Furiae than any other. Members of high standing have served gloriously in the navy or gone into the Ministry of Asmodeus.

It is unclear how the deaths of so many prominent members will affect city affairs, but High Ruler Ovida Cascare says that the Corano estate will be handled smoothly and the city will rebound quickly from this tragic loss.

"We still know so little about our current surroundings," said Griffin spokesperson Gynara Forge. "We hope to begin mapping the local Outlands to further the interests of our noble houses, expand property allowances and usable farmland, and benefit all of Furiae."

Indeed, the Arrival caused several of Furiae's noble houses to lose access to significant land holdings on our borders with the Great Kingdom, and without the farms and estates outside the city limits, Furiae has had to rely more and more on foreign trade. If the city is to survive, and thrive, its holdings must expand.

There is also talk of specific places of interest in the surrounding area, rumours brought to the city by local travellers; the Griffin Bank may hope to recover items of interest as part of their return on investment for this expedition.
Interested parties should inquire at the bank with a complete resume of past expedition and adventuring experience.
Yesterday, unknown assailants slaughtered several members of the Fraternity of Order in a Midtown municipal building.

The Fraternity, one of the factions that came to Furiae in the years since the Arrival, is devoted to understanding law and has aided Furiae's civil functions as record-keepers, lawyers, and judges. These members managed and guarded a building in Midtown that housed legal records and other important documents.

Late yesterday, they were found murdered inside the building. Investigators cannot place a specific motive for the murders: some documents in the building seem to have been accessed, but such documents are not kept under lock and key so motive has been hard to pin down.
A suspect was seen leaving the scene shortly after the incident is believed to have occurred. Any information on this event should be brought immediately to the City Guard.
House Corano Assassinated! "This is an attack against all Furiae."
Furiae Sentinel, Vol. 32, Issue 132 - News in the Gauntleted City

It was Lady Ovida Cascare and the other noble houses who saved our fair city from the chaos of dangerous anarchists and untrustworthy foreigners. The High Houses' deal with the denizens of the Nine Hells was meant to ensure our safety -- baatezu peacekeepers, a crushed rebellion, and eventually a safe place in the realm of Avernus.

Anticipated amongst the celebration are the execution of a swathe of recently-captured anarchists, public whippings, a military parade, and one of the Lifeblood Theater's famed blood plays. Be sure to bring a coat if you're in the splash zone!
As a reminder, all servants, slaves, service workers, taxis, and entertainers are expected to do their civic duty and work during the festivities.

We have not yet obtained the safety we were guaranteed. We have not reached the land we were promised, rebels and anarchists still stalk the alleys, and the devil guard has waned in effectiveness and morale. Are the devils failing to follow the terms of their own contract? Why has their focus gone elsewhere? How are we citizens of Furiae meant to feel safe and secure?

The baatezu are creatures of law. They must be made to see the responsibilities they owe us, the terms of the contract we entered with them. Ovida and the nobility must stand up to Zariel, the leader of Avernus, and demand the safety were promised, as is our contractual right!
House Cascare has issued an official missive today for the populace of Furiae. All citizens are reminded of their civic duty to help keep law and order in our fair city.
If your hear of any revolutionary pursuits, illegal activity (including the use of illicit substances), or treasonous whispers, report them immediately to city authorities.
You will be rewarded for your loyalty and service. Our city will be safer for it.
Despite recent hardships across the city, Furiae institutions are buzzing with anticipation as preparations are already underway for the annual Tax Day festivities.

This classic Furiae holiday has persisted for decades in the city, surviving independence from the Great Kingdom, the treacherous civil war within our own walls, and the Arrival. Not just the day when collectors visit all citizens of Furiae for the annual taxation that keeps our city running, it is also an official, celebrated, holiday.
Many citizens will not be expected to work on this day, and festival activities, performances, street food, and more will be available throughout the city.
Editorial: Devils Not Living Up to Their Promises?
City Prepares for Next Week's Festival

We here at the Furiae Sentinel would like to formally apologize for yesterday's editorial. The opinions expressed within it are not the opinions of this newssheet. The work escaped the eyes of our censors, but the writer will certainly no longer be contributing to this publication -- nor any publication.
The warehouse was being operated by a known planar trader, Ulan Aurintar. Aurintar too was found on the scene, murdered in his own place of business.

City Guard investigators have uncovered a horrific scene in the North Market neighborhood. Several eviscerated bodies were found in the basement of an unassuming apartment, including a woman who was once a spiritual advisor to House Corano.

The scene was a bloody one, with several of the corpses having clearly been cut open prior ro the deaths of the victims. This horrible, unsanctioned act has the Guard questioning whether there is a serial killer stalking the streets of Furiae.
Given the death of the spiritual advisor, a woman known as Aladara, some are wondering if it is connected to the assassinations of the Corano family mere days ago.

Investigators and Harmonium agents are keeping their eyes open for any other indicators of this serial killer. Citizens are cautioned not to let strangers into their houses, to lock your doors at all times, and to report any suspicious activity to law enforcement immediately.

After the tragedy that struck House Corano two days ago, with several key members of the family assassinated in an attack against the city itself, House Vivadan has stepped up to assist the beleaguered noble family.

No longer able to handle all of their previous holdings, Corano has sold their interest in the Lifeblood Theater -- known for its patriotic performances -- to House Vivadan, who have promised to hold to the Theater's storied traditions.
House Vivadan has already announced a grand performance in honor of House Corano, in a few weeks time.

We are in full support of our alliance with the devils, and are sure that the rulers of our city will ensure a continued positive relationship with our benefactor and patron, Zariel. We, and indeed all, citizens humbly await our reward of safety, security, and protection in Avernus.
House Erogoth and House Hamalus have brought competing bids to the Court of Furiae to re-open the quarry west of the city.

Seemingly abandoned before the Arrival, the quarry has sat empty for long enough, say representatives of each house. To stay prepared against any act of war from the planes, we must keep our economy -- and fortifications -- strong.
Both houses have submitted bids for the land, which otherwise has been claimed by the Furiae government as no legal deed can be found.

Yesterday in the Sea Market, unknown assailants broke into a dockside warehouse and massacred everyone who was unfortunate enough to be on the scene. Authorities have discovered this cowardly act of terrorism to be the work of rebel elements in the city.
The warehouse was being operated by a known planar trader, Ulan Aurintar. Aurintar has not been seen since the attack, and authorities fear him dead as well.

Merchants and travellers all over the district -- and indeed, the city -- are wondering if their legitimate enterprises could be targeted next. What horrific lengths will these rebels and anarchists go to in order to sow chaos?

They clearly have no sympathy for the common citizen of Furiae, who depends on the commerce of the market for stability and prosperity. These revolutionary forces must be brought to justice! Citizens are encouraged to report any rebel activity to the authorities.
Businesses Attacked -- Merchants Wonder If They're Next

Yesterday, opposing groups of mercenaries fought to the death in the halls and rooms of the infamous Soul Trade Inn. Authorities arrived on the scene to help maintain order at the venerable establishment.

There has been much banter bandied about regarding the recent reception of the street substance known as "worldwine". Many perceive it a plague on our people, reducing restless and bereft residents to mindless mannequins who merely accept all that fate foists upon them in their dreamlike dazes.

These vocal and virtue-signalling viewers prefer to place blame on the affected for falling into their fugue state, vehemently vowing that these victims deserve all the visitation and vice overrunning the vicinity! But *victims* is what this new potion's purchasers are: victims of a vile system that subjugates those civilians unable to survive under its shackles. Victims who should be vindicated.
If you have caught yourself blaming the buzzed Rathole boarders, I understand the impulse, but resist!

As we well know, unemployment is a massive and meaningful matter for the city. The Baatezu and House Cascare would have you thanking them for their newfound tolerance of travel and trade in the Outlands. These measures matter to the moneyed and imminent, but remain out of reach for the masses.

For some, it must be understood, worldwine is the only relief they can find in a city that seeks to sink and subsume them entirely. It is sad, yes, but it cannot be condemned as evil. That label must be reserved for those who put us in this position in the first place!

Further clouding the context, even though only one group guards the method and means to mete out more worldwine, price per potion proceeds to precipitously plummet. Why? This syndicate's savagely savvy sales strategy is centered on showering a stricken and strapped society with a swiftly (but shortly) satisfying substance. A substance they'll soon find they can't survive the next day without.

Put plainly, this potent pharmaceutical -- worldwine -- is the only affordable escape at hand for our most dispossessed denizens. Let us not judge them so harshly; let us judge the society that scorned them.
WORLDWINE -- PROVIDING NECESSARY RELIEF FOR SOME
Regret reaches the Rag today as renowned revolutionary Regiallan "Reggie" Reillico was removed from the ranks of the rebels.
Known for nothing less than nine noteworthy fights with Furiae forces during the pre-Arrival rebellion, Reggie remained devoted to defiance despite the devils in our post-Arrival predicament.

Alas, almost a year ago, the vigilante vanished from his veranda. Friends of the paper postulated the Secret Police were perhaps to blame, after a years-long yearning to arrest, arraign, and make him answer for his actions.
We must assume that in the year since, Reggie was subjected to Questioning and Torture; the length of that imprisonment gives us hope that he held out against his enemies.

Our new planar position also provides hope that he has a happy future despite death. Proof that we persist post-death exists in the Petitioners, and we wish Reggie an exciting existence in the Domain of Trithereon, wherever it may be.
SAD DAY AS RENOWNED REVOLUTIONARY EXECUTED
Yesterday, several members of House Corano, one of the Largest Local Landowners, were ASSASSINATED.
By all accounts, the murders were bloody, and included Two Children! What Manner of Monster would mandate such a heinous and horrendous happenstance?
Why, none other than our own ostensibly righteous rulers, the cowardly Cascares!

Cascare has long loomed large over our fragile Furiae, and though both houses had a hand in the deadly deal with the devils during the Pre-Arrival civil war, the Cascares have yearly yearned for increased influence in the matters material such as the navy and economic estates and events!

Ridding themselves of their rivals in House Corano, who have holdings throughout the city and garner great favour in the mighty military, gives them greater political power in Furiae and in the eyes of the ever-present evils, perhaps pushing us closer to permanent participation in the plots of Avernus.

Even now they scramble to secure safety from Sigilian Support -- an angle enviously opposed by the Coranos. What manner of evil are they cooking up in their roosts high above the common man's homes? Dare we wait to find out?
HOUSE CORANO ASSASSINATED -- MAKES WAY FOR CASCARE POWER GRAB
The fight for freedom in Furiae has acquired an additional ally.

Yesterday, a slaver's safehouse was Assailed and Assaulted. The despicable degenerates profiting on the sale of mortal lives have largely been slain and will slave no more. Just one of an assortment of such slavery operations in this city, yes, but no doubt a start.

Yesterday, someone put a stop to an odious operation in the North Market neighbourhood. Someone was OPERATING on helpless slaves, seemingly solely for pleasure. But that soulless savage has been stopped. Though no victims survived, there will be no more.

Yesterday, someone put a stop to an odious operation in the North Market neighbourhood. Someone was OPERATING on helpless slaves, seemingly solely for pleasure. But that soulless savage has been stopped. The surviving victims are safe.

These events seem not to be associated to any specific revolutionary exercise, but are certainly welcomed by us at the Rag. Does Furiae have a new vigilante on its streets? Can we anticipate more actions like this? Or was this an isolated incident with more monstrous motives?
Only time will tell, but we are hopeful that we really do have a new warrior for the cause of true justice!
All across our urban apartments, residents have had restless reposes recently. Many informants notify us that nightmares are the source of the sleeplessness!

One woman who works with folks who wet their whistle with worldwine reports relatively greater restlessness among those vulnerable voices. Dreamlike days have descended into evening insomnia. Worldwine users wake woefully.

This must be a malignant means of stopping the spread of the substance by our devilish despots, perhaps a profane punishment! What rituals do their warlocks recite to remove the substance -- indeed, whole spectrums of civilians -- from the streets?

We must resist the resulting tightening of the fist of fascism, for Furiae will fail without the fearless survival of its set-upon citizens. Stand against the servants of evil. Do what you must to survive.

I've been thinking, these past few years, about our position, our relationship with our... benefactors. How the original deal was crafted.

My thoughts bend toward our ultimate destination, Avernus. We would have power, as we were guaranteed. There we would claim our reward, our promised transformation into something much more than human. But the safety we were told would also be ours, I question. It is not a *safe* place.

It is a blasted landscape of near constant war. Machines of death driven across the wasteland by fiends of every description. An atmosphere thick with brimstone and tar, swarms of flesh-eating bugs, deadly sandstorms. Even given newfound power and eternal life, do you really think we could *thrive* there?

Here, however, in the Outlands, we yet may. For whatever reason we have not yet slipped into Hell. There is a growing contingent of the minor houses -- those who did not sign into the deal, those houses who gain little from our future kingdom in Avernus but the safety we sold them -- who think we're best off here. Trade, wealth, power. I have to say, I'm beginning to agree with them -- contract be damned.

It is curious -- the Sea Market provides excellent evidence of how a looser grip replaces and even *increases* the wealth of the houses, yet so many would still opt for tighter control when we have so many more options now. Perhaps we could forge a new deal with a different benefactor who could see us free of the yoke of He...

Mog has fled you and the city in a flurry and magic and curses. In this reservoir, surrounded by stores of worldwine, a choice falls to you.

Worldwine is poisonous to all outsiders, regardless of their inherent immunities. Dumping the worldwine into the reservoir will possibly loosen -- if not break -- the devil's hold on Furiae. It could have untold consequences, but maybe they will be worth it.
Slowly, you pack up what materials and worldwine you can, thinking of the gold you will be able to extract from the city above...

Slowly, you tip each barrel and container over into the rushing water, as the hag would have done -- but she can't feed on the dreams of the afflicted anymore. You wonder how the city will change as you watch the worldwine swirl away...

But there is also a lot of potential gold to be had here. There is enough worldwine to last quite some time and turn a tidy profit. Through your investigation, you have a ready-made model to start distribution. Even with a finite stock, the profits would last you the rest of your natural life without a worry.

Worldwine has been a terrible plague on Furiae. With production being rare, if not impossible to replicate again, destroying this store would eliminate worldwine from ever being a threat to anyone -- outsider or addict -- again.

The revolutionaries of the city could find a use for even a limited supply of worldwine, a substance that can poison outsiders. It could be a potent weapon in the fight against the devils that help hold a grip on Furiae.

The city guard would also want custody of such a large stock of this dangerous arcane substance. There are secrets here that would greatly aid law enforcement, from the store of worldwine, to the distribution network, to the very existence of the tunnels. You would doubtless be greatly rewarded.
Slowly, you pack up what materials and worldwine you can, thinking about how Furiae will change with this substance in the hands of the city...
Slowly, you pack up what materials and worldwine you can, thinking about how the city will be affected with this substance in the hands of the revolutionaries...
You set to work smashing what containers remain, burning ingredients and coating the cave floor with it. You ensure no one ever gets their hands on this substance again...
Dump the worldwine in the water.
Take it to the City Guard.

As for Mog she has returned back to wherever she came from, to reunite with her sisters, apparently.  No matter who she was, she held enough knowledge of the planes and its substances to craft and enchant something as powerful as worldwine.

Thankfully, she is gone -- but enough of the recipe for worldwine is out there. A substance that can cause poison-like symptoms in outsiders, who are typically immune to such things, could have far reaching consequences... You can only hope that no one else has the skill, dark knowledge, and raw ambition that Mog did. There is nothing you can do now but hope she now lacks the resources to recreate it.

Many of the former users of worldwine are forced to take in the realities of their despotic city. Because of this the revolutionaries, despite losing a potential weapon against the devils, see an increase in recruitment. You continue on with your own life, knowing that the city is safe from the threat of worldwine from here on out.

The temptation of riches born from worldwine was too much much to bear. You'd already demonstrated your ability to take an organization like this apart and it left you with the contacts, streetsmarts, and knowledge to build one back up.
After the heat of the investigation dies down you manage to make contact with Harasi in order to arrange a new distribution network. The woman is nothing if not business-minded.

It doesn't take long to set up a new network. It also doesn't take long for the remaining supply of worldwine to run out. Without the ability to make more to feed the demand, you decide it's time to get out of the business -- and Furiae -- leaving the city to deal with the aftermath on its own.

Shortly after your exodus from Furiae, having paid a fair fee to smuggle yourself out by ship, you hear rumors about the Prime city dealing with crime and riots, the devil rulers cracking down, harsher than ever. You decide it's not your problem anymore, if it ever was.
Some of the agents of Harasi's distribution network, mentioned in her notes, remain in the city, and it's fairly easy to track them down and offer them work.

It takes a few days after you resolve to empty the remaining worldwine into Furiae's aquifer to see the effects. But effects there are. In the following weeks, productivity takes a sharp downturn as the populace deals with the effects of the substance in the water supply -- even diluted, it creates a dreamlike pall over the city.

For their part, the devils are forced to retreat to Hellroost and other strongholds for several weeks before the water is declared "safe." Rumors circle that several of them started weakening and becoming sick, a state that the immortal creatures have never had to deal with.

It didn't take long for the Revolutionary element in the city to notice and, while it wasn't enough of an effect to foment open rebellion in Furiae once again, they were able to take more than one devil off the board. While harsh punishments were meted out in several corners of the city, the devils are forced to stay out of the public eye for some time.

With the devils out of commission for the moment, Lady Ovida was forced to open the door even further to outsiders, bringing in more Harmonium to help with cleanup and control. With them came others: Anarchs, looking to help free the city; Sensates, looking to experience the waves of a culture in flux; Indeps, looking for trade and adventure. With the new influx of visitors, the grip of the Gauntleted Fist loosened in some areas of the city. Perhaps wresting Furiae even further from Avernus' control.

Otherwise, the city continues as it has since it found its new home. For now, it seems the fallen angel Zariel is distracted -- something pulls her attention away from this lost prize. But what if that attention returns?
The ripples of your actions will help create the wave that carries the city into its future. And what shape does that future take?

Such a question can only be answered by citizens of Furiae like you. The Gauntleted City, staring into the very mouth of Avernus, persists in the Outlands, full of stories and intrigue, citizens and rebels, law and chaos. Its future is unclear, but the eyes of the planes are upon it. What manner of stories will they see play out as Furiae moves into an uncertain future among the planes? Only time will tell.

After being detained for a full week, the City Guard lets you go, satisfied that you actually had nothing to do with the sale and production of worldwine. You are given a small reward for your work, a medal presented by the Guard (under the watchful presence of a devil) in a very small ceremony in the Teeth of Orisaw.

Your fame is short-lived after the Sentinel reports that the City Guard was responsible for ending the threat, and insinuates blame on the rebel forces still present in the city. For your part you do what the law and your city demands, and try not to pay attention to the rumors flying around the Sea Market that agents of House Cascare have been experimenting with what remains of the worldwine stock... nor think about whether the city has drifted closer to Avernus.

The revolutionaries you turned your worldwine samples over to gratefully accept it, and quickly bring you before one of the coordinators of the local cells. After detailing all of the information you gathered on your investigation, from incriminating documents and notes to the location of the last of the stocks of worldwine hidden under Furiae, you are dismissed with a sum of gold, grateful thanks, and a vow of silence.

You return to your life, much the same as it was before, albeit a bit more comfortable with some extra gold in your pocket. You also find yourself having to pay less at market. Locals, gruff before, give you a respectful nod. At taverns, your drink is usually filled first. You aren't sure what became of the rest of the worldwine, but you have heard rumors that the revolutionaries are quietly experimenting with it. It seems like it's only a matter of time before worldwine makes an appearance in Furiae once again...

Even though the brass of the City Guard claims most of the credit for taking worldwine off the streets, you remain content in the knowledge that you did what you thought was best. After a few very tense weeks of near riots by citizenry from all walks of life dependent on the arcane substance, Furiae settles back into its usual routine.
